![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212195/assets/cf9fda11d138a5227307070d52fc0a27ce9decc35c91efbb026b89d4507f2ce7.png)

A beverage is pumped into a conical dispenser at a constant rate of  $19.6\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}\text{/min}.$ The mouth of the tank is $70\,\text{cm}$ in diameter and the height of the tank is $40\,\text{cm}.$ How fast is the beverage level increasing when the volume of the beverage in the dispenser is $12.25\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the dimensions of the tank. Let's call $H=40\,\text{cm}$ the height of the tank, and $R=\frac{70}{2}=35\,\text{cm}$ its radius at the top. These quantities are fixed and do not change with time.

Now, let's consider the solution level. We call $h$ the solution level's height and $r$ the radius of the cone formed by the solution. Both of these quantities, and the solution volume $v,$ change with time. In particular, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=19.6\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{min},
$$

and we want to find $\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}$ when $v=12.25\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$

We need to find a relation between $h$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $v.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $r$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $r$ in terms of $h.$

Note that the cones formed by the tank and the solution must be similar. Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{R}{H} \\ \frac{r}{h} & =\frac{35}{40} \\ r & =\frac{7h}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {(\frac{7h}{8})}^{2}h \\  & =\frac{49}{192}\pi {h}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we have an equation relating $v$ and $h,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{49}{192}\pi {h}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{49}{64}\pi {h}^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the rate at which the level of the beverage in the dispenser is changing when $v=12.25\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$ We can compute the value of $h$ at this moment as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}12.25\pi  & =\frac{49}{192}\pi {h}^{3} \\ {h}^{3} & =48 \\ h & =2\sqrt[3]{6}\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug in the known values into the formula for $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}19.6\pi  & =\frac{49}{64}\pi (2\sqrt[3]{6})^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ 19.6\pi  & =\frac{49\sqrt[3]{36}}{16}\pi \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & ≈1.94\,\text{cm}/\text{min}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the solution level is increasing at a rate of approximately $1.94\,\text{cm}/\text{min}.$
